title: Staged signature index and synthetic-canary for quant profile drift detection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: We onboard multiple quantized variants (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) for the same model family. Current onboarding pushes artifacts and perf profiles directly to the pin registry and relies on real traffic canaries to detect regressions — this is slow and noisy. We need an automated staged-commit flow that a) fingerprints quant artifacts with a deterministic signature, b) runs a synthetic-workload canary suite (latency, p99, token cost, generation-quality sketch) against dedicated staging shards, and c) publishes an indexed performance signature that can be used for fast drift detection and automated rollback.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each quant artifact published has a canonical signature (hash of weights + metadata) and a searchable index entry.
design_decisions:
- Use content-addressable signature: sha256(weights_blob) + model_config_version + quant_metadata.
- Store signature + minimal perf vectors in the 'quant-signature-index' in S3 (parquet) and expose via internal catalog API.
- Synthetic canary workload will exercise prefix lengths {8,32,128,512}, streaming and non-streaming paths, and the KV-cache warm/cold states.
- Define a compact perf vector: {latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, sample_bleu_delta, hallucination_count_sample}.
- Canary run produces pass/fail vs baseline with thresholds configurable per-model family.
- Publish a 'canary-report' artifact linking signature -> perf vector -> telemetry snapshot.
implementation_notes:
Phase 1 (MVP):
- Hook into quant ingestion pipeline to compute signature at artifact publish time.
- Launch ephemeral staging shards pre-provisioned for canary runs (reuse Dedicated staging pool).
- Run canary harness (existing perf harness adapted) for 10 synthetic prompts per prefix length.
- Compute delta vs pinned baseline; if any metric regresses beyond thresholds, mark artifact as 'blocked' and emit regression alert.
Phase 2:
- Integrate with pin registry to store signature and a 'quality_score' and enable filter by signature on rollouts.
- Add automated nightly sampling of in-prod traffic to validate synthetic signals.
operational_runbook:
- On publish, pipeline emits: signature file, canary-report.json, perf-vector.csv.
- If canary fails: auto-block promotion, open ENG ticket with 'canary-failure' label, notify quant-owners on Slack #quant-onboarding.
- For false positives: provide 're-run canary' with --seed and --deterministic flags.
- Emergency rollback: Coordinator service can pin previous signature and apply runtime fallback to a compatible unquantized variant.
metrics_and_thresholds:
- latency_p95 delta: fail if > 10% and > 25ms absolute.
- p99: fail if > 15% and > 50ms absolute.
- tokens_per_sec: fail if < 90% of baseline.
- BLEU/quality sketch: fail if sample_bleu_delta < -1.5.
- Hallucination count (sample of 50): fail if > 2 more than baseline.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Synthetic canary may miss real-world distributional issues. Mitigation: Phase 2 adds sampled in-prod traffic validation and periodic shadow comparisons.
- Risk: Signature collisions across different quant formats due to metadata mismatch. Mitigation: include quant-algorithm id + params in canonical signature and validate on ingestion.
- Risk: Increased staging costs. Mitigation: run canaries on small spot pool with strict time budget and batch canonicalization runs.
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Created ticket after on-call surfaced a quant rollout with a silent 30% p99 regression — need faster detection than warm canaries.

2025-02-14 Liam O'Connor: Spike completed for signature format and a local harness run. Observed that KV-cache cold path amplifies p99 regressions for AWQ variants — we'll include KV warm/cold permutations in canary.

2025-02-21 Priya Rao (ML Eng): Added draft synthetic prompt corpus focusing on instruction-following and retrieval-style prompts. Suggest expanding to low-entropy prompts for hallucination sensitivity.
2025-02-25 Design review (Alex Torres): UX for pin registry view needs a compact 'quality_score' and a link to canary reports. Logged DES-412 for dashboard refinement.

2025-02-28 Liam O'Connor: Initial S3 index prototype pushed (PR#1425). Running nightly smoke canaries against INT8/GPTQ families. Early results: INT8 baseline passes, AWQ shows consistent 12% tokens_per_sec drop at 512 tokens. Triage meeting 2025-03-03 scheduled.
2025-03-01 Maya Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to include searchable index requirement and canary artifact publishing.
